components.css: .ds-score{color:var(--color-fg);font-family:Geist,sans-serif;}.ds-score-num{display:flex;align-items:baseline;gap:8px;margin:0;}.ds-score-num span{font:500 clamp(4rem,10vw,6rem)/1 'Geist Mono',monospace;letter-spacing:-0.04em;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;color:var(--color-pass);}.ds-score-num small{font:400 20px 'Geist Mono',monospace;color:var(--color-subtle);}.ds-score h2{margin:12px 0 32px;font:600 24px/32px Geist,sans-serif;letter-spacing:-0.025em;}.ds-score ul{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:14px;}.ds-score li{display:grid;grid-template-columns:110px 1fr 36px;align-items:center;gap:16px;font-size:14px;}.ds-score li span{color:var(--color-muted);}.ds-score i{height:6px;border-radius:9999px;background:var(--color-line);overflow:hidden;}.ds-score b{display:block;height:100%;border-radius:9999px;transform-origin:left;animation:ds-fill 900ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) both;}.ds-score em{font:normal 500 14px 'Geist Mono',monospace;text-align:right;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;}@keyframes ds-fill{from{transform:scaleX(0);}}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-score b{animation:none;}}

narrative.overview:
Scanly presents a resume review the way a deploy dashboard presents a build: a single result, stated plainly, with the log and the evidence one glance away. The ground is near-black, surfaces separate by hairline borders rather than shadow, and the only voices allowed to carry color are interaction (blue) and the score bands (green, amber, red). Everything else is grayscale text on gray hairlines, so a colored number is always a verdict and never decoration.

Density is product-UI dense, not marketing-airy: 14px body, 36px controls, rows of 12px vertical padding, one container at 1024px. Type is Geist for language and Geist Mono for every number, so scores, sizes, timers, and file names read as measurements. The pinned reference is Vercel's product UI; the build follows it in material (hairlines, white primary button, mono numerals) and refuses the pastel-gradient SaaS card grid with score rings.

Motion is nearly absent by design. There is one authored animation (score bars fill once when a review opens) plus functional feedback: color transitions on hover, a spinner, skeleton pulses. All of it yields to `prefers-reduced-motion`.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground, hairline borders, flat surfaces.
White primary button; blue reserved for focus and active interaction.
Green/amber/red mean score band and nothing else (one exception: the destructive confirm).
Every number set in Geist Mono with tabular figures.
Verdict before evidence: the score and a plain sentence lead every review.

rules.name: The Band-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red appear only where `scoreTone` assigns them: score numbers, score bars, and tip/log status icons. Fail Red additionally marks error text, which is the same meaning (failed). Destructive Red appears on the destructive confirm button and nowhere else.

rules.name: The Blue Is a Cursor Rule
rules.body: Blue marks where the user is acting (focus, drag, selection, caret). Links and buttons do not turn blue; links go from muted to fg on hover.

rules.name: The Thresholds Live in One Place Rule
rules.body: Score bands are pass at 70 and above, warn at 50 to 69, fail below 50, defined once in `scoreTone`. Never re-derive them in a component.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Mono Rule
rules.body: Any score, count, size, timer, or file name renders in Geist Mono with tabular figures. Prose never does.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Headings and labels are sentence case at normal tracking. No uppercase, letter-spaced labels.

rules.name: The Hairline, Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Panels, rows, fields, and buttons separate by a 1px Hairline border and a tonal step. Shadows are reserved for content that sits above the page (modals).

dos: **Do** color a number only through `scoreTone`: pass at 70 and above, warn at 50 to 69, fail below 50.
**Do** set every score, count, size, and timer in Geist Mono with tabular figures.
**Do** separate surfaces with a 1px Hairline (#262626) border and a tonal step, not a shadow.
**Do** lead any review surface with the score and a plain verdict sentence, evidence after.
**Do** keep one Paper White primary button per view; everything else is secondary or icon.
**Do** gate any new motion behind `prefers-reduced-motion`, as the bar fill and upload scroll already are.
donts: **Don't** use blue for links, fills, or content highlights; it marks focus, drag, selection, and caret only.
**Don't** use green, amber, or red for decoration, categories, or branding; red as a fill is only for the destructive confirm.
**Don't** draw score rings or gauges; scores are a big mono number and flat horizontal bars.
**Don't** add gradients, pastel tints, or a card grid for the review history; it is a divided list in one panel.
**Don't** add uppercase letter-spaced labels or small headings above headings.
**Don't** add shadows to panels, rows, or buttons; the modal is the only lifted surface.
